The more audit partners and managers are involved in supervising and reviewing audit engagements, the better the audits tend to be, according to new research from the University at Buffalo School of Management.

more.title: What 2024's record-breaking rainfall says about the next El Niño
more.summary: Though strong El Niños have occurred only four times in as many decades, 2024's intense El Niño is already getting a sequel. New UCLA research shows that 2024 broke the record for extreme rainfall, with 40% of that increase tied to global warming—and conditions are ripe for a repeat.

more.title: Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence?
more.author: Natalie Wolchover
more.summary: A mathematical mechanism enables AI models to process language at scale, undergirding the current AI revolution. Our columnist asks: Why is attention the key? The post Is ‘Attention’ the Essence of Intelligence? first appeared on Quanta Magazine

more.title: Meet the Anthropic Engineer Keeping Its AI Agent Trustworthy
more.author: Amanda Davis
more.summary: If you’ve ever wondered how Claude and similar AI agents can answer complex questions in seconds and where they get the information, you’re not alone. Gurmeet Saran works to find that answer every day as an engineer at Anthropic in San Francisco, the AI research company behind Claude.

more.title: Smart ring maker Ultrahuman to roll out biological-age model across UAE
more.author: Jagmeet Singh
more.summary: Ultrahuman and Abu Dhabi will spend the next two years working on research and clinical validation of the model.

more.title: First Utility-Scale Enhanced Geothermal Plant Goes Live
more.author: Maria Gallucci
more.summary: This article was originally published by Canary Media . The geothermal startup Fervo Energy is now selling power to the grid from its Cape Station project in Utah — marking the first time a utility-scale, next-generation geothermal facility has achieved such a feat worldwide. The Houston-based firm turned on an initial 33-megawatt unit late last week and has been testing and ramping up output since then.

A program offering low-income Maryland households inexpensive loans for rooftop solar and energy efficiency. These are just some of the recent projects…

more.title: Magnetic sculpting transforms single-source fields into predetermined shapes with mathematical precision
more.summary: Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties.

more.title: Electoral integrity under pressure as elections faced persistent threats in 2025
more.summary: Elections across the world faced a wide range of pressures on electoral integrity in 2025, from violence and misinformation and disinformation to electoral management malfunctions, cyberattacks and natural hazards, according to a new report.

more.title: Nanostructure-assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment
more.summary: Parkinson's disease (PD) is one of the most common neurological disorders associated with later life, and its prevalence rises sharply with age. It affects the brain systems that control movement, often causing tremor, stiffness, slowness and problems with balance, all of which can reduce independence and quality of life in older adults.

more.title: Chemical disorder gives new ceramic film magnetic properties for potential low-power electronics
more.summary: A material thinner than a human hair may foster faster computing devices that demand less energy and store more data, according to a multi-institutional team led by researchers in the Penn State College of Earth and Mineral Sciences.

more.title: From nonmagnetic to magnetic: A 2D semiconductor with electrically tunable magnetism
more.summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore (NUS), in collaboration with scientists from institutions in Switzerland, the Czech Republic and Germany, have demonstrated a way to introduce magnetism into an otherwise nonmagnetic two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor and subsequently control its magnetic properties using an electrical voltage.

more.title: Reinforced vertebrae allow plunge-diving seabirds to survive high-speed impact
more.summary: A northern gannet scans the sea for fish from 100 feet (30 meters) in the air. Upon seeing a school, it pitches its body into a nosedive, somehow breaking the surface at 70 miles per hour (113 kilometers per hour) without breaking its neck. This daring maneuver seems to defy the laws of nature, but it's standard hunting behavior for plunge-diving seabirds.

more.title: Measuring wildfire plumes to predict extreme fire behavior
more.summary: Predicting the unpredictable starts with understanding how extreme wildfires develop and under what conditions. This knowledge is essential to better anticipate and respond to them. To achieve this, firefighter and researcher Marc Castellnou and the GRAF/Bombers Catalonia team measure the atmosphere both inside and outside wildfire plumes.

more.title: Cholesterol-linked drug boosts gene-targeting potency in early findings
more.summary: Nucleic acid therapeutics, such as antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), have emerged as promising platforms for treating a variety of previously hard-to-treat diseases, including neurological diseases.

more.title: High-speed microscopy captures sugar-building enzymes forming rigid pairs and flexible assemblies
more.summary: From a rigid molecular pair to flexible assemblies with moving domains, the enzymes that build sugar chains display strikingly different behaviors.

more.title: Major cities worldwide are sinking, satellite data reveal
more.summary: Land subsidence is the gradual sinking of the ground, which can damage buildings, foundations, and drainage and sewage systems, and may increase flood risks. However, information on land subsidence dynamics remains limited, which makes it difficult for policymakers to identify where risks are intensifying and where urgent intervention may be needed.
